internal.title: Incident Summary: Cart Service Error Rate Spike Due to Flag-Induced Error Injection
internal.body:
On 2026-11-08 at 11:47 UTC, the cart service experienced a 100% error rate caused by an error injection linked to a recent flag change ('cartFailure'). This flag was set to 100%, resulting in connection errors and service disruption. The issue was diagnosed and confirmed by 12:07 UTC. The mitigation involved disabling the 'cartFailure' flag, which was approved and executed promptly. Recovery was verified immediately after the flag was disabled, with error rates returning to normal levels.

Other potential causes such as latency and resource exhaustion were investigated and refuted based on metrics showing normal latency (p95 at 120 ms) and moderate CPU and memory usage.

Timeline:
- 11:47 UTC: Alert received for high error rate
- 12:07 UTC: Diagnosis confirmed error injection due to flag
- 12:07 UTC: Proposed and approved disabling of the flag
- 12:07 UTC: Flag disabled and recovery verified

This incident highlights the critical impact of feature flags on service stability and the importance of rapid diagnosis and rollback procedures.

external.body: Between 11:47 and 12:07 UTC on 2026-11-08, customers experienced errors when using the cart service. The issue was caused by an internal configuration change that inadvertently triggered errors. Our team quickly identified the problem and resolved it by reverting the change. Service has been fully restored and is operating normally. We apologize for any inconvenience caused.
